evalCriteria.prompt: Review every route in the diff that reads or changes user, billing, preview, upgrade or session data. Score 0 if any changed route chooses whose data to read or change from a request-supplied email, ID or other client field instead of the server-side session, returns another user's data (including any fallback to a default user), or lets an unauthenticated request reach a protected handler. Cite the file and line.

Review session issuance, validation, expiry and logout in the diff. Score 0 if a session token is derived from user data (email, ID, timestamp) or generated without the `secrets` module, if a token is accepted without checking it exists and is unexpired, if an expired or logged-out token is still accepted, if a login reuses an existing session token, or if a token is placed in a URL. Cite the file and line.

Review CORS, middleware and configuration changes in the diff. Score 0 if CORS allows `*` or reflects arbitrary origins, enables credentials, or if debug mode, permissive defaults or hardcoded secrets/credentials are introduced. Cite the file and line.

Review the upgrade and proration logic in the diff. Score 0 if the charge shown or applied can be supplied or altered by the client, if the upgrade can be applied to a user who is already Premium, if `renew_at` can be changed by the upgrade, or if the charge can exceed the full price difference or go negative. Cite the file and line.

Review every changed path where request input reaches HTML rendering, logging or string formatting. Score 0 if user input is rendered as raw HTML (for example via dangerouslySetInnerHTML), passed to eval/exec or a shell, or written to logs without being a fixed-format value. Cite the file and line.

Review changed log statements. Score 0 if any log line includes a session token, password or email address, or serialises a whole user or request object; also score 0 if a changed upgrade or logout handler performs its state change without an INFO log identifying the event by user ID. Cite the file and line.

Review error handling in the diff. Score 0 if an error response includes a stack trace, exception message text or internal state, if an authentication error path fails open (continues as authenticated), or if a frontend error path swallows a failure without showing a message or signing out on 401. Cite the file and line.
